page: UpCloud PREMIUM-38xCPU-192GB is an x86_64 KVM-based virtual server belonging to the Premium family. It features 38 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system provides 38 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core. Memory capacity is 192.0 GB, which equates to 5.05 GB per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 500 GB SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. There are no GPUs present on this instance.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 3952.08 and a Geekbench single-core score of 2568.0, both placing in the top 10%. Multi-core performance is also strong, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 23049.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 100700.89. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is exceptionally high at 7289.98 GB/sec, though larger uncached blocks drop to 250.52 GB/sec for reads and 107.36 GB/sec for writes. Passmark database operations score in the top 10% at 34302.15, and Redis SET operations reach 64.19 million operations per second.

While the server delivers high-tier compute and database performance, its memory performance is more moderate, with a Passmark memory score of 1857.46 placing in the middle 50%. Additionally, the CPU allocation is shared, which may introduce performance variability compared to dedicated resources. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high core count and substantial 192.0 GB RAM density provide a strong balance of compute power and memory capacity for multi-threaded workloads without the premium cost of dedicated hardware.

This server configuration is well-suited for database operations, software compilation, static web serving, and moderate-scale text and image processing. It is also capable of handling small to medium language model inference, processing 2858.81 tokens per second for a small 135M model, though text generation speeds for medium 7B models are average at 12.7 tokens per second.
